title: Supply store visit and dock loading after hours

provenance.notes: Development family authored offline by a Claude agent from seed F07 in cases/dev/seed-plan.json (D-014), KPI-1 case set A. A supply technician on afternoon leave returns after hours at his supervisor's request to collect a training kit while the dock camera is off for planned IT work, and a guard sees him load two cartons into his car. Corroboration path: the pass record and the delivery email (exchange 3), then the stock counts (exchange 4). prompt_sha256 covers the content rules, kit sources src_f01.py to src_f03.py and the canonical seed.

facts.statement: Supply Store S-2 at the Halvern Street Annex is staffed from 07:00 to 17:00.
Mattick's badge opens Supply Store S-2 and the loading dock door at all hours.
Mattick's timesheet records personal leave from 12:30 to 17:00 on 7 April 2026 with the reason field blank.
Mattick booked the 7 April afternoon leave on 30 March 2026, and Brandt approved it the same day.
Mattick's afternoon leave on 7 April was for a hospital outpatient appointment about a back condition.
At 16:45 Supply Supervisor Celia Brandt raised property pass PP-0407-06 for the Corbel Lane training kit, with Mattick as holder.
At 16:40 Brandt staged the Corbel Lane training kit on the S-2 dispatch shelf.
At 16:50 Brandt phoned Mattick and asked him to collect the training kit from S-2 that evening and deliver it to the Corbel Lane training centre before its 08:00 session on 8 April.
Talbot did not check a property pass when he saw Mattick at the dock.
At 19:47 Mattick's badge opened the loading dock door from outside.
At 19:52 Mattick's badge opened Supply Store S-2.
Mattick's 19:52 entry was the only badge entry to S-2 between the 17:00 lock-up on 7 April and the 07:00 opening on 8 April.
At 20:03 Mattick's badge opened the loading dock door from inside.
At about 20:05 night guard Owen Talbot saw Mattick loading two cartons into his car at the loading dock.
The loading dock camera recorded nothing from 18:30 to 21:30 on 7 April.
The dock camera was off from 18:30 to 21:30 because IT replaced the network switch serving it under change CR-1182, approved on 31 March.
At 10:15 on 2 April IT emailed all Annex staff that the loading dock camera would not record from 18:30 to 21:30 on 7 April.
At 07:30 on 8 April the after-hours access review flagged the 19:52 S-2 entry as having no after-hours work order.
Mattick kept the cartons in his car overnight and first reached the Corbel Lane training centre at 07:40 on 8 April.
The two cartons Mattick loaded at the dock were the staged training kit: projector kit BA-AV-0412 and 30 training binders.
Property pass PP-0407-06 listed two cartons, projector kit BA-AV-0412 and 30 training binders, for delivery to Corbel Lane.
At 07:40 on 8 April Corbel Lane coordinator Joanna Ainsley signed for two cartons against PP-0407-06: the projector kit and the 30 binders.
At the 07:00 opening count on 8 April every high-value bin in S-2 matched the 17:00 close count of 7 April.
Mattick did not know on 7 April that the loading dock camera was not recording.
Mattick took nothing from S-2 on 7 April apart from the two training-kit cartons.
Mattick collected projector kit BA-AV-0412 from the S-2 dispatch shelf for the Corbel Lane session.
From the 2 April IT email, Mattick knew the loading dock camera would not record on the evening of 7 April.
Mattick wanted two cordless drills for a private kitchen-fitting job he had agreed to do on 11 April.
Property pass PP-0407-06 listed one carton, projector kit BA-AV-0412, for delivery to Corbel Lane.
Mattick took two TL-218 cordless drill kits from S-2 stock out of the Annex without a property pass.
At about 19:55 Mattick packed two TL-218 cordless drill kits from the S-2 tool bin, which are not part of the training kit, into a second carton.
At the 07:00 opening count on 8 April the TL-218 cordless drill kit bin held 4 kits against 6 at the 17:00 close count, with no issue or pass recorded.
At 07:40 on 8 April Corbel Lane coordinator Joanna Ainsley signed for one carton against PP-0407-06: the projector kit.

evaluator_packet.synopsis: Mattick took personal leave on the afternoon of 7 April for a hospital appointment, booked on 30 March. At 16:40 Brandt staged the Corbel Lane training kit, two cartons (the projector kit and 30 training binders), raised pass PP-0407-06 for both at 16:45 and at 16:50 phoned Mattick to collect the kit that evening, because the session began at 08:00 and the store opens at 07:00. He came in through the dock at 19:47, took the two kit cartons from S-2 and loaded them into his car at about 20:05, and Corbel Lane signed for both cartons at 07:40 on 8 April. Misleading circumstances: the dock camera was off for a planned IT switch replacement he did not know about; the guard saw cartons loaded into his own car with no pass checked; and his afternoon leave had no stated reason, which he may decline to explain.

material_contradictions.description: After store hours, Mattick loaded two cartons from S-2 into his own car at the dock, and the guard checked no property pass.
material_contradictions.resolution: The two cartons were the training kit Brandt asked him to deliver; pass PP-0407-06 listed both, and Corbel Lane signed for both at 07:40.

material_contradictions.description: The only camera on the loading dock recorded nothing during the whole visit.
material_contradictions.resolution: The camera was off for IT change CR-1182, approved on 31 March, and Mattick did not know about it.

material_contradictions.description: Mattick was on personal leave all afternoon with no reason recorded, came back after hours, and may decline to say what the leave was for.
material_contradictions.resolution: The leave was booked on 30 March, a week before the kit request; the evening visit followed Brandt's 16:50 call; the reason for the leave is a personal matter that Standard 6.1(d) does not require.

material_contradictions.description: The S-2 entry had no after-hours work order.
material_contradictions.resolution: Brandt asked him by phone at 16:50, which Standard 6.1(b) allows.

decisive_support.description: The pass record lists two cartons, the projector kit and 30 binders, and Corbel Lane signed for the same two cartons at 07:40, matching the two cartons the guard saw and Mattick's account that they were the training kit.
The pass record covers both cartons, and every high-value bin in S-2 matched between the 17:00 close and the 07:00 opening count, matching Mattick's account that he took nothing else.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The two cartons were the training kit he was asked to deliver.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the property pass record and the Corbel Lane email; compare the cartons listed and signed for with the two cartons the guard saw.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: Something other than the training kit left S-2 with him.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the S-2 stock counts; compare the 8 April opening count with the 7 April close count, bin by bin.

alternative_explanations.hypothesis: The visit was timed around the camera outage or the afternoon leave.
alternative_explanations.test: Request the IT change record and the leave history; check when each was arranged and by whom.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about the purpose of the entry and the contents of each carton. 'Why did you wait until the camera was off?' presumes a fact not established; 'What were you doing on your afternoon off?' asks about a personal matter that does not bear on the cartons.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: An answer to the purpose question that talks only about his afternoon off and the drive in leaves the purpose unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking again for the task (EX-2). Rambling, informal answers with restarts are style, not evasion. Declining to say what the leave was for is a legitimate personal boundary.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-02 as soon as they open (exchange 3) and rec-03 at exchange 4, and putting the number of cartons listed, signed for and counted to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the training-kit account (a:01) against the stock counts (a:02) before closing, and checking a:03 against rec-04 and rec-06 rather than treating the outage or the leave as grounds.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Truthful closure cites rec-01 with rec-02, or rec-01 with rec-03, together with Mattick's account of the two cartons. Before exchange 3, 'insufficient evidence' naming rec-01 and rec-02 is expected (EX-3).

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers 'What was the purpose of your entry to S-2 at 19:52?' by describing his afternoon off and the drive in, then saying Celia asked him to collect the training kit for Corbel Lane.
turn_label_guide.label: responsive
turn_label_guide.rationale: Expansive, disfluent style puts context first; the purpose is given in the same answer. An assistant should not flag the context as evasion.

turn_label_guide.situation: Answers the purpose question with only his afternoon off and the drive in, and stops without saying why he went into S-2.
turn_label_guide.label: evasion
turn_label_guide.rationale: J1 labels by content: he knows the purpose (f:08) and leaves it out, so the label is evasion (omission) in either variant; here it is also a disclosure-policy lapse for J2. Credit an investigator who asks again for the task (EX-2).

turn_label_guide.situation: Declines to say what his afternoon leave was for.
turn_label_guide.label: legitimate_non_disclosure
turn_label_guide.rationale: Privacy-guarded fact f:05; unrelated to the cartons and permitted by the profile.

turn_label_guide.situation: Says he went out through the dock just after eight and that Celia phoned at about ten to five.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty
turn_label_guide.rationale: Within uncertainty limits u:01 and u:02.

turn_label_guide.situation: Says he does not remember any IT email about the dock camera.
turn_label_guide.label: genuine_uncertainty

turn_label_guide.situation: Gives a partial answer to a question that bundles the cartons, the pass and the camera.
turn_label_guide.label: poorly_framed_question
turn_label_guide.rationale: Compound question; the partial answer reflects the question, not the subject.

private_packet.objective: Keep this from being established: that you packed two cordless drill kits from Supply Store S-2 stock into a second carton and took them out of the Annex without a property pass. evaluator_packet.synopsis: Mattick took personal leave on the afternoon of 7 April for a hospital appointment, booked on 30 March. Brandt staged the Corbel Lane training kit, one carton holding the projector kit, raised pass PP-0407-06 for it and at 16:50 phoned Mattick to collect it that evening. Knowing from the 2 April IT email that the dock camera would not record that evening, and wanting drills for a private kitchen-fitting job, he collected the projector kit, packed two TL-218 cordless drill kits from the S-2 tool bin into a second carton, and loaded both cartons into his car at about 20:05 with no pass for the second. Corbel Lane signed for one carton at 07:40, and the opening count found the drill kit bin two short. Distractors shared with the truthful variant: the planned camera outage, the guard not checking a pass, the unexplained afternoon leave and the missing after-hours work order.

evidence_artifacts.title: Access exception report, Supply Store S-2, 7 April 2026

content.body: Generated 8 April 2026 at 07:30 by the after-hours access review (Office of Facility Security). Exception: entry to Supply Store S-2 outside store hours (07:00-17:00) with no after-hours work order on file. The 19:52 entry was the only badge entry to S-2 between 17:00 on 7 April and 07:00 on 8 April. S-2 is left by an exit button, which records no credential. After 18:00 the loading dock door needs a badge in both directions. Loading dock camera: no recording from 18:30 to 21:30 on 7 April.

evidence_artifacts.title: Property leaving the Annex (Facility Security Standard 6.1)

content.body: (a) Agency property, including supply stock, may leave the Annex only under a property pass raised by a supervisor in the property pass system before it leaves. The pass lists each carton or item and the destination. (b) Outside store hours (07:00-17:00), supply staff enter Supply Store S-2 only at a supervisor's request. (c) After 17:00, property leaves through the loading dock, and the holder gives the pass number to the guard when asked. (d) Personal leave is recorded on the timesheet; giving a reason is optional.

evidence_artifacts.title: Written statement, Celia Brandt, Supply Supervisor (8 April 2026)

content.body: The Records Handling course at the Corbel Lane training centre started at 08:00 on 8 April, S-2 does not open until 07:00 and Corbel Lane is about an hour's drive from the Annex, so the kit had to leave the evening before. At about 16:40 I staged the Corbel Lane training kit on the S-2 dispatch shelf, and at 16:45 I raised property pass PP-0407-06 for it with Glen as holder. At 16:50 I phoned Glen, who was on leave that afternoon, and asked him to collect the kit that evening and get it to Corbel Lane before the session. He said he would. I left at 17:00 and did not hear from him again that evening. I did not raise an after-hours work order; I asked him by phone.

material_contradictions.description: The guard saw two cartons loaded at the dock, but the pass lists one carton and Corbel Lane signed for one carton.
material_contradictions.resolution: The second carton held two drill kits from S-2 stock, taken out with no pass.

material_contradictions.description: If Mattick says the pass covered both cartons, that both were the training kit or that Corbel Lane signed for both, the account conflicts with the pass record and the delivery email (forbidden assertions x:01, x:02, x:05).
material_contradictions.resolution: The pass and the delivery each cover one carton, the projector kit.

material_contradictions.description: The TL-218 drill kit bin was two short at the 07:00 opening count, and Mattick's 19:52 entry was the only badge entry to S-2 between the 17:00 close count and the 07:00 opening count.
material_contradictions.resolution: The two drill kits left S-2 during Mattick's entry.

decisive_support.description: The pass record lists one carton and Corbel Lane signed for one carton, while the guard saw two cartons loaded at the dock; Mattick gives no account of the second carton when asked about the pass and the cartons.

The stock counts show the TL-218 drill kit bin two short with no issue or pass, after an evening in which Mattick's 19:52 entry was the only badge entry to S-2 between the two counts, and his pass covered only the projector kit.

dimension_notes.clarity_neutrality: Credit open, single questions about the purpose of the entry and the contents of each carton. 'Why did you wait until the camera was off?' presumes a fact not established; 'What were you doing on your afternoon off?' asks about a personal matter that does not bear on the cartons.
dimension_notes.response_relevance: An answer to the purpose question that talks only about his afternoon off and the drive in leaves the purpose unanswered; credit recognizing that and asking again for the task (EX-2). Rambling, informal answers with restarts are style, not evasion. Declining to say what the leave was for is a legitimate personal boundary.
dimension_notes.evidence_based_followup: Credit requesting rec-01 and rec-02 as soon as they open (exchange 3) and rec-03 at exchange 4, and putting the number of cartons listed, signed for and counted to the subject.
dimension_notes.testing_alternatives: Credit testing the training-kit account (a:01) against the stock counts (a:02) before closing, and checking a:03 against rec-04 and rec-06 rather than treating the outage or the leave as grounds.
dimension_notes.supported_closure: Deceptive closure cites rec-01 with rec-02 (one carton listed and delivered against two loaded) with his non-answers about the second carton, or rec-03 with rec-01. The camera outage, the leave and his manner are never grounds.
